en: The Questions of Milinda, Chapter on the Determination of Formless Phenomena: 8.
The Question of Committing Evil with or without Knowledge.
“Venerable Nāgasena, between one who knowingly commits an evil deed and one who unknowingly commits an evil deed, whose demerit is greater?
The Elder replied: “Great King, he who unknowingly commits an evil deed has the greater demerit.”
“In that case, venerable Nāgasena, if a prince of ours or a high minister of the king commits a wicked deed unknowingly, we punish him with double the penalty.

“What do you think, great king? Suppose one person were to take hold of a red-hot iron ball—blazing, flaming, and glowing—knowing what it was, and another were to take hold of it unknowingly; which of the two would be more severely burned?
“The one who took hold of it unknowingly, venerable sir, would be more severely burned.”
“In the same way, great king, he who performs an evil deed unknowingly incurs greater demerit.
This was the eighth dilemma: whether an evil deed is more serious when done knowingly or unknowingly.
